info.title: Report API
info.description:
Read-only financial reports of a Bkper Book, from a request in any language or a Bkper query. Report never creates, changes or deletes anything in a Book.

## Show a person a report

When a person asks to see a report of a Book (expenses, revenue, income versus expenses, profit and loss, balances, by category, by month, …), unless they ask for a custom report (see Custom reports), call `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report` with:

```json
{ "prompt": "<the person's request, in their own words and language>", "format": "html" }
```

and give them the returned file as it is: one self-contained, interactive HTML report (the answer with its comparison to the previous period, a chart with small previews of every other chart that fits, to switch to in place, a breakdown table whose rows open in place, and its source: the period and the exact Bkper query) that loads nothing and links to the same report in the Report app; shown by the Bkper Agent in a Book, that link opens it in Report in place of the Agent. With the Bkper CLI, save it and publish the file:

```bash
bkper app api request report /api/v1/books/<bookId>/report -d '{"prompt":"show my expenses by category this year","format":"html"}' > report.html
```

This one call is the whole task, and the deterministic route to the report: every amount is a Bkper balance of one group or Account, as Bkper shows it, read by code, never by AI; Report adds nothing up, but for one labelled case below, and the file shows the exact Bkper query it read, for anyone to audit. So do not compute or query the balances yourself, do not ask for `format: spec` first, and do not re-check the amounts or open the file: publish it and answer in a line, as the report speaks for itself. `format: spec` (the default) is the JSON Report's own web client renders; showing a report never needs it.

## Custom reports

A request for a custom report, or one that says it is not for the Report app, is not for Report: build that report yourself from the Book's Bkper balances (with the Bkper CLI or API), and do not call `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`. Report's own **Custom report** chip opens the Bkper Agent with such a request started, in the person's language, such as "Create a custom report, without using the Report app, that …". Every other report request goes to Report as above.

## What a request can ask

- One top-level (root) group of the Book, such as Expenses or Assets, broken down into the subgroups and Accounts Bkper returns; or income versus expenses (the net result).
- A subgroup or an Account, by its name as the Book writes it (case and accents aside), such as "Food this year"; or several, such as "Food and Rent by month" or "Food versus Rent": each with its own balance side by side, never added up. They must all be balances (Asset, Liability) or all activity (Incoming, Outgoing), else `mixed_targets`. Keep the names in the prompt as the person wrote them. A request that writes no name of the Book reports the subgroup or Account it means, else the root group it is about; groups the Book hides only when named.
- The net result comes from the group that combines the Book's Incoming and Outgoing groups, as Bkper calculates it. Without one, when each activity root is only Incoming or only Outgoing and no two share an Account, Report subtracts the Outgoing roots from the Incoming roots and labels the result "Calculated by Report". Otherwise the Book has no net result (`no_net_result`) until income and expenses meet in one top-level group.
- A period in whole months: this or last month, quarter or year, the year before last, year to date, the last 12 months, all time, any year, quarter or month the person writes, or today. Without one: activity this year, balances today, or the last year with movements in Books with old data. One that has not started, such as next month, is `future_period`.
- What the period is compared with: the previous period, the same period a year earlier, or any other period of the same kind the prompt names (last year vs 2023, Q3 vs Q1). A comparison that cannot be made, such as a month against a year, compares with the previous period instead and says so in the report.
- By month, or a breakdown, a trend or a total.
- A chart, when the person names one: a donut (a pie is drawn as one), bars, a line, an area, stacked by month, versus the previous period, or no chart. Keep it in the prompt as they said it. A line for activity, or bars for balances, replaces the usual chart by month. A chart that does not fit the numbers (such as a donut with a part below zero, or a bridge, which Report never draws) is not drawn: the report shows the closest chart that fits and a line under its title says why. Every chart that fits is offered as a preview beside the report's title (at most six), so there is no need to ask again for another chart.
- A `#hashtag`: only transactions with it. One per report, as Bkper filters balances by one; a prompt's first hashtag is read and the others are left out.

Activity groups (Incoming, Outgoing) report what moved within the period; balance groups (Asset, Liability) report the balance at its end; a balance today, or at the end of a month, also shows a line of the 12 month-ends ending then. Balances may be up to 60 seconds old.

## Report a Bkper query

To report what a Book shows, send its Bkper query as `query` instead of `prompt`; a person's words always go as `prompt`. A `prompt` with a `group:`, `account:` or `acc:` term is read as a query too. A query is read exactly as sent, with no AI: every amount is Bkper's balance for that very query, as the Book's sidebar shows it, future-dated transactions included, and nothing in it is rewritten or cut off. Its `group:` and `account:` names are what the report is of (several side by side, up to six); its period is the days Bkper read (`after:01/01/2026 before:01/01/2027` is Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2026; `before:` alone, a balance as of its last day; no dates, all time). Months for charts come from the same query by month, and the comparison from the same query with its dates moved to the period before; each is left out unless it reads as the query does. The report's `text` is the query, which sent back as `prompt` is read as that query. A query that names no group or Account Bkper finds answers 422 `query_not_a_report`.

## Saved prompts

`/api/v1/books/{bookId}/prompts` is a Book-shared shelf of original prompts, not computed reports. `GET` lists `prompts: [{ id, prompt }]` in the shelf's order and fresh `capabilities: { list, save, remove, move }`. Every known non-`NONE` role may list, including `RECORDER`; only `OWNER` and `EDITOR` may save, remove or move. `POST` accepts exactly `{ "prompt": "…" }` and returns the saved `{ id, prompt }` (200), a new prompt last and one saved again in its place; `DELETE /api/v1/books/{bookId}/prompts/{promptId}` returns 204, including when absent; `PUT /api/v1/books/{bookId}/prompts/{promptId}/position` accepts exactly `{ "before": "<id>" | null }` (`null`: the end) and returns the whole shelf in its new order, as `GET` does (404 `prompt_not_found`, 409 `shelf_changed` when `before` is gone: list again). All three are idempotent for identical input.

Save only when asked: this writes durable app metadata shared with the Book's collaborators, not Book resources or executable saved queries. Only the original text is saved (edges trimmed, 1–1000 characters), never report HTML, resolved intent, dates, amounts, inferred language or a separately selected chart. To open one against current data, send its `prompt` to the existing singular `POST /report`. Every shelf operation reads the Book's role afresh. Native saved-query role permissions apply, but its owner-plan billing restriction is not inherited. Storage visibility is eventually consistent; independent items cannot overwrite each other, while concurrent save/remove of the same item follows KV ordering. Shelf responses must not be cached. A 502 `storage_error` means retry the same operation; a failed write may have reached storage.

## Errors

Errors are JSON, `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message" } }`. With `not_a_report`, the request names nothing this Book can report: ask the person to name a group of the Book and a period, or offer the reports it carries as `suggestions` (those `GET /api/v1/books/{bookId}/suggestions` lists): each is a request, built with no AI when sent as `prompt` exactly as listed, in the same `language`. Four errors are problems of the Book itself, with a `problem` object naming what is involved: `empty_book` (no transactions yet), `nothing_to_report` (no groups, or most Accounts with transactions in no group), `no_net_result` (no group combines its income and expense groups, or they share Accounts) and `mixed_group` (the group asked for mixes balances with activity). `GET /api/v1/books/{bookId}/suggestions` tells the first two as `problem` when the Book opens. Report never changes the Book: if the person is its OWNER or EDITOR (`problem.canOrganize`), offer to organize its groups for them (for `empty_book`, to help them get started), changing groups only, never transactions, and only once they agree; otherwise, tell them to ask the Book's owner.

get.description: Checks that the API is reachable. Not needed before other calls.

Up to three reports this Book can have, the main one first, each as a request a person would type, in `language`: the Book’s groups at its first two levels, each as its natural report (income and expenses together this year, income or expenses by month, balances today), ranked by Bkper AI once each time the groups change. Periods: activity this year, or the last year with movements when this year has none (the text names that year), and balances today. Use them when the person does not know what to ask, or after `not_a_report`; to build one, send it as `prompt`, with the same `language`, and, to show it, `format: html` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`: exactly a suggestion’s text (spacing aside, case kept) is built with no AI. When the Book has no reports at all, there are none and `problem` tells why: `empty_book` (no transactions yet) or `nothing_to_report` (no groups, or most Accounts with transactions in no group); if the person may (`problem.canOrganize`), offer to help organize its groups, changing groups only, never transactions. Read-only.

post.summary: Build a financial report of a Book from a request in any language or a query
post.description:
Builds a financial report of the Book: of one of its root groups (such as Expenses or Assets, with its subgroups and Accounts), of a group or Account the prompt names, of several side by side, or of income versus expenses, over a period of whole months, by month or not, optionally only for one `#hashtag`. Read-only: the Book is never changed.

To show a person a report, send `{ "prompt": "<their request, in their own words and language>", "format": "html" }` and give them the returned HTML file as it is: it is self-contained and interactive. With the Bkper CLI: `bkper app api request report /api/v1/books/<bookId>/report -d '{"prompt":"…","format":"html"}' > report.html`, then publish `report.html`. That one call is the whole task: do not ask for `spec` first, query the balances yourself or re-check the amounts; every amount is a Bkper balance read by code, and the file shows the query it read.

With `format: spec` (the default) the report is the JSON Report’s own web client renders: its spec (with the data of every chart that fits), text, language, query, data time, chart and link. `text` is the report’s own short text in its language; sent back as `prompt` with its `language` (and the chart asked for, `chart.asked`, as `chart`), it asks for the same report, and `chart` shows it as another chart. A suggestion’s text sent as `prompt` builds the report without AI.

To follow what a Book shows, send its Bkper query as `query` instead of `prompt`: it is read exactly as sent, with no AI, so every amount is the one Bkper’s sidebar shows for that query (future-dated transactions included), its period is the days Bkper read, and its `text` is the query. A `prompt` with a `group:`, `account:` or `acc:` term is read as a query too. A query that names no group or Account Bkper finds answers `query_not_a_report`.

Every amount is a Bkper balance of one group or Account, as Bkper returns it (but a net result Report calculates, labelled so), read by deterministic code; balances may be up to 60 seconds old. Code finds in the prompt the exact names of the Book’s groups and Accounts it writes, and its first `#hashtag` (Bkper filters balances by one); AI only recognizes the root group when the prompt writes no such name, the parts of the period it says (how long, which year, month and quarter, and those of a period it compares with; never a date), whether it asks about months, parts, an earlier period or a bridge, and which chart it names; code decides the report and its charts from those judgments and the numbers.

Every script and style is inline and it loads nothing, so it works in a sandboxed frame: the chart shows tooltips, previews of every other chart that fits show it in place, rows open in place, and a link opens the report, as the chart chosen, in the Report app (shown by the Bkper Agent in a Book, in place of the Agent).

422.description: Not a report this Book can have (`not_a_report`, with `suggestions` to offer instead), a `query`, or a `prompt` read as one, that names no group or Account of the Book, or none Bkper finds (`query_not_a_report`), a period that has not started (`future_period`), groups or Accounts side by side that mix balances with activity (`mixed_targets`), a net result the Book does not have (`no_net_result`: no group combines its Incoming and Outgoing groups, or they share Accounts), a group that mixes balances with activity (`mixed_group`), or a Book with no reports at all (`empty_book`: no transactions yet; `nothing_to_report`: no groups to report on). The last four carry `problem`: what is involved and whether the person may organize the Book’s groups (`canOrganize`), which fixes all but `empty_book`; offer it, changing groups only, never transactions

get.summary: List the Book’s shared saved prompts and current capabilities
get.description: Lists original requests shared by every collaborator of this Book, including RECORDER. This is the saved-prompt shelf; POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report builds a report. Authorization reads the Book afresh, never the balances cache. Every storage page is read; visibility is eventually consistent. This never computes a report or changes the Book. Responses must not be cached.

post.summary: Save an original prompt on the Book’s shared shelf
post.description: Requires OWNER or EDITOR, checked afresh. Saves only the trimmed original prompt and its opaque id in durable app metadata, not in the Book’s executable saved-query list. Identical text after edge trimming is idempotent across collaborators. Does not store HTML, resolved intent, dates, numbers, inferred language or a separately selected chart. No AI or report computation runs. Native saved-query role permissions apply, but its owner-plan billing restriction is not inherited. Independent items never overwrite each other; visibility and concurrent changes to the same item follow KV eventual consistency. A later save can save a removed prompt again.

delete.summary: Remove a prompt from the Book’s shared shelf
delete.description: Requires OWNER or EDITOR, checked afresh. Either may remove any saved prompt on this Book. Idempotent: an absent id also succeeds. Removes only this item of app metadata, never a report, a Book saved query or financial data. Visibility is eventually consistent. A failed write may have reached storage, so retrying the same removal is safe.

put.summary: Move a prompt on the Book’s shared shelf
put.description: Requires OWNER or EDITOR, checked afresh. Puts the saved prompt just before `before`, or at the end for `null`, and answers the whole shelf in its new order, as the list does. Already in place, nothing is written. Only this prompt’s place changes; prompts saved before the shelf had an order get one on the first move, in the order they had. Never changes a prompt’s text, a report or the Book. Visibility is eventually consistent, so a list right after may not show the move yet; the response is the order this request wrote. Retrying the same move is safe.

code.description: What failed: `invalid_request` (400, the message names the field), `unauthorized` (401, no valid Bkper token), `forbidden` (403, the person cannot view the Book), `not_found` (404, no such API route), `book_not_found` (404, no such Book, or not shared with the person), `not_a_report` (422, the request names nothing this Book can report: ask for a root group or income versus expenses with a period, or send a suggestion), `query_not_a_report` (422, the `query`, or a `prompt` read as one, names no group or Account of the Book, or none Bkper finds), `future_period` (422, the period has not started), `mixed_targets` (422, the groups or Accounts the prompt names side by side mix balances at a date, Asset and Liability, with activity in a period, Incoming and Outgoing: ask for them in separate reports), `no_net_result` (422, the Book has no net result: no group combines its Incoming and Outgoing groups, or its activity groups share Accounts; organizing its groups fixes it), `empty_book` (422, the Book has no transactions yet), `nothing_to_report` (422, the Book has no groups, or most of its Accounts with transactions are in no group; organizing them into groups fixes it), `mixed_group` (422, the group asked for holds both balances, Asset or Liability, and activity, Incoming or Outgoing; separating them into groups of their own fixes it), `ai_allowance_exhausted` (429, the person’s Bkper AI allowance is used up: suggestions sent as they are still work), `upstream_error` (502, Bkper or Bkper AI failed: try again) or `internal_error` (500).

message.description: What failed, in English, for people and logs. Never the request text.
message.example: Book not found, or not shared with you.

suggestions.description: Up to three reports of the Book’s own groups, the main one first; none with a `problem`.

SuggestionsResponse.description: Suggested reports; or, when the Book has no reports at all, none and `problem`: `empty_book` (no transactions yet) or `nothing_to_report` (no groups to report on). Every report request of that Book then answers the same 422 error.

ungrouped.description: Accounts with transactions that are in no group.

bookName.description: The Book’s name, as Bkper writes it.

canOrganize.description: Whether the person may change the Book’s groups (OWNER or EDITOR), so they, or an agent for them, can fix it. Otherwise only the Book’s owner can.

code.description: No group combines the Book’s Incoming and Outgoing groups, and its activity groups cannot be netted: they share Accounts, or some hold neither kind alone.

incoming.description: Names of the activity root groups holding Incoming Accounts, in Book order.

outgoing.description: Names of the activity root groups holding Outgoing Accounts, in Book order.

shared.description: Names of the activity root groups that share Accounts with another, in Book order; empty when none do.

bookName.description: The Book’s name, as Bkper writes it.

canOrganize.description: Whether the person may change the Book’s groups (OWNER or EDITOR), so they, or an agent for them, can fix it. Otherwise only the Book’s owner can.

code.description: The group asked for holds Accounts with transactions of both balances (Asset, Liability) and activity (Incoming, Outgoing).

BookProblem.description: Why the Book cannot have the report, found by fixed rules from its groups and Accounts, and what is involved. Every case but `empty_book` is fixed by organizing the Book’s groups, never its transactions.

names.description: Every group and Account of the Book’s balances, each once, in Book order: root groups in order, each with its subgroups, then its Accounts, then the Accounts in no group. Archived Accounts with no balance are left out.

id.description: Id of the group or Account, as in `bkper group list` and `bkper account list`.

name.description: The name as the Book writes it.

root.description: Id of its root (top-level) group: itself for a root group or an Account in no group; for an Account in several root groups, the first in Book order.

BookName.description: A group or Account of the Book, by name.

language.description: The Bkper language of the report’s texts.

query.description: The Bkper query of exactly the report’s transactions and dates, the one its balances were read with, to list them or check balances in Bkper; of a `query`, that query as sent. Relative periods keep Bkper’s date variables (`$y`, `$m`, `$d`), which Bkper resolves from the Book’s today.

dataAt.description: When the balances were read (ISO 8601); they may be up to 60 seconds old.

kind.description: The chart in the spec: `bar`, `line`, `area` or `stacked` by month; `ranked-bar` or `donut` of the parts; `compare` (each part against the previous period); `none` for no chart. `waterfall` is no longer given.

fallback.description: True when the chart asked for (`asked`) does not fit this report, so `kind` is the closest chart that fits, or the one the report picks; the spec’s `Report` `notice` says why.

asked.description: The chart asked for: the request’s `chart`, else the one its `prompt` names (`donut` for a pie); left out when none was. The report’s `text` never names it, so send it as `chart` with the `text` to show the report the same way again.

chart.description: The chart drawn, and the one asked for, if any.

text.description: The report’s own short text, in `language`, as a person would type it: what it is of, how it is shown when by month, its period as asked (relative periods stay relative, such as `this year`) and what it is compared with, and its hashtag; of a `query`, the query itself. Send it as `prompt` to ask for the same report again, or show it to the person to edit.

url.description: The same report in the Report app, to open or share with the person.

ReportSpec.description: The report as a flat json-render spec (`root` and `elements`) of the Report catalog, every text in `language`: `Report` (title, period, the `request` it answers as a person would type it, its period as asked, and a `notice` when it could not compare, or draw the chart asked for, as asked, with why) holds `Answer` (amount, previous period amount and change; one per group or Account shown side by side, in order, with none for them together), `Chart` (when one fits), `Visualizations` (every chart that fits, at most six, each but the main one with its data), `BreakdownTable` (the subgroups and Accounts Bkper returns, with amount, share and change, nested; for a net result Report calculates, its roots and a total; side by side, the groups and Accounts shown, with no total) and `Source` (with `calculated` when Report calculated the net result). Every amount is a Bkper balance of one group or Account, as Bkper returns it, but a net result Report calculates. Amounts and ratios are exact decimal strings; months and instants are ISO.

items.description: A report this Book can have, as a person would ask for it, in the language of the suggestions. Send it as `prompt` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`, with the same `language`: exactly this text (spacing aside, case kept) builds it with no AI.

suggestions.description: With `not_a_report`: reports this Book can have, to offer the person instead; send one as `prompt`, with the same `language`, to build it with no AI.

ReportErrorResponse.description: An error of a report request; with `not_a_report`, `suggestions`; with `empty_book`, `nothing_to_report`, `no_net_result` and `mixed_group`, `problem`: what is involved, and whether the person may organize the Book’s groups.

prompt.description: The report the person asked for, in their own words and language: do not translate it. Include what they said about the period, the view, the chart and a `#hashtag` (only the first is read, as Bkper filters balances by one); leave out the Book’s name or id, which the path gives. Names of the Book’s groups and Accounts written exactly (case and accents aside) are reported as such, several side by side. Uses one Bkper AI decision; a suggestion of `GET /api/v1/books/{bookId}/suggestions`, sent as it is (spacing aside, case kept) with the same `language` (else `Accept-Language`, else English), uses none, and so does a Bkper query (a text with a `group:`, `account:` or `acc:` term, such as a query report’s own `text`), which is read as `query`.
prompt.example: show my expenses by category this year

query.description: Instead of `prompt`: a Bkper query, such as the one a Book shows its transactions with, read exactly as sent, with no AI: every amount the report shows is Bkper’s balance for that very query, as the Book’s sidebar shows it, future-dated transactions included; nothing is rewritten or cut off. Its `group:` and `account:` names (case and accents aside) are what the report is of, several side by side (up to six, the first found); names the Book does not have, or Bkper does not find, are left out, and with none the answer is 422 `query_not_a_report`. Its period is the days Bkper read, as written (`after:01/01/2026 before:01/01/2027` is Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2026; `before:` alone, a balance as of its last day; no dates, all time). Months for charts come from the same query by month (`by:m`), only when Bkper gives it the same totals; the comparison, from the same query with its dates moved to the period before, only when it has an end. The report’s `text` is the query itself.

chart.description: The chart to show, over any the request names: how to show the report, not what it is, so its `text` never names it. `bar`, `line`, `area` or `stacked` by month (`line` for activity, or `bar` for a balance, in place of the usual one); `ranked-bar` or `donut` of the parts (`pie` is drawn as `donut`); `compare` (each part against the period compared with); `table` (no chart); `auto` (the report picks). A chart that does not fit the report is not drawn: the report shows the closest chart that fits, else the one it picks, and a line under its title says why (`waterfall` never fits). To reopen a report as the person last saw it, send its `text` with its `language` and the chart they chose.

language.description: Language of the report’s texts, as a BCP 47 tag of one of the 133 Bkper languages, such as `pt` or `pt-BR`. Leave it out to write the report in the language of `prompt`, else `Accept-Language`, else English.

format.description: What to return. `html` to show the report to a person: one self-contained, interactive HTML file (`text/html`) that loads nothing and links to the report in the Report app; save it and publish or share it as it is, without asking for `spec` first or re-checking its amounts. `spec` (the default) for JSON, which Report’s own web client renders: the report as a json-render spec with its text, language, query, data time, chart and link.

ReportRequest.description: Exactly one of `prompt` (the person’s request, in any language, or a suggestion’s or a report’s own `text`) or `query` (a Bkper query). Usually `{ "prompt": "…", "format": "html" }`.

prompts.description: All saved prompts in the shelf’s order: a new prompt goes last, and moves change it. The server follows every storage page. Visibility after saves, removals and moves is eventually consistent.

list.description: True for OWNER, EDITOR, POSTER, RECORDER and VIEWER. Unknown or NONE roles are denied.

save.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR.

remove.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR; either may remove any prompt on this Book’s shelf.

move.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR; either may reorder any prompt on this Book’s shelf.

capabilities.description: Freshly authorized capabilities, not a substitute for authorization on the next request. Native saved-query role rules apply; its owner-plan billing restriction is not inherited by app metadata.

id.description: Opaque saved-prompt id returned by this API. Scoped to the Book.

prompt.description: Only the saved request text. To build it against current Book data, send this as `prompt` to the singular POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report.

SavedPrompt.description: Book-shared original prompt, not a report snapshot or executable saved query. No HTML, intent, resolved period, amounts, inferred language or separately selected chart is saved.

prompt.description: The original request, in its own words and language. Trimmed at the edges, 1–1000 characters; internal whitespace and case are preserved. No report is computed and no AI is called.

before.description: The id of the saved prompt this one goes just before, or `null` for the end. Take it from the latest list; an id no longer on the shelf answers 409 `shelf_changed`.
